The post Community Bankers Sue OCC Over Crypto Firms' National Trust Charters appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) has sued the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC). The October 2 complaint alleges the OCC lacks the power to charter non-fiduciary crypto firms as national trust banks.

The lawsuit was filed in federal court in Washington, D.C. It also names Comptroller Jonathan Gould in his official capacity. It asks the court to strike down the 2026 rule and 2021 guidance behind the OCC’s crypto charter approvals.

What ICBA Wants the Court to Undo

The complaint targets three OCC actions. They include the March 2026 final rule, Interpretive Letter 1176 from January 2021, and Protego’s conditional approval. Protego received that approval in February 2026.

According to the filing, Gould authored the 2021 letter as the OCC’s senior deputy comptroller and chief counsel.

ICBA says the OCC misread a 1978 amendment to the National Bank Act. That reading, it argues, lets the OCC charter trust banks that neither take deposits nor act as fiduciaries.

The group also cites the major questions doctrine, saying such broad power needs clear approval from Congress. It calls the rule arbitrary and capricious as well, noting the OCC gave commenters only a two-page response.

The 2021 letter, ICBA adds, skipped the public notice and comment process that federal law requires.

ICBA wants the rule, the letter, and Protego’s approval vacated. It asks the court to bar the OCC from using either policy to grant or conditionally approve any charter.

The Crypto Firms Already Holding OCC Approvals

The complaint says the OCC has approved or conditionally approved 21 trust banks under the Trump administration. At least 13 are crypto companies, though the filing names only Protego.

OCC decisions and company announcements show which digital asset firms have won approvals since December 2025.

  • December 2025 brought conditional approvals for Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets, and Paxos. Circle won final approval in July.
  • February 2026 added conditional approvals for Stripe-owned Bridge, Crypto.com, and Protego.
  • Coinbase followed on April 2, and Nomura’s digital asset arm Laser Digital on May 29.
  • World Liberty Trust Company, backed by the Trump family, received conditional approval in August.
  • Agora, Catena Labs, and Bastion won conditional approvals on September 18.

ICBA President and CEO Rebeca Romero Rainey framed the case around consumer protection.

“American consumers reasonably expect a federally chartered bank to carry federal protections. Digital assets held at a crypto firm operating under a national trust charter do not carry those important safeguards,” he said.

The suit also arrives before the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act takes effect. ICBA argues that the law, effective by January 18, 2027, cannot cure charters the OCC has already granted.

item.content:encoded:
President Trump is weighing Jay Clayton, the former SEC chairman who sued Ripple, for the role of White House AI czar.

That possibility has unsettled parts of the crypto community, which is still watching Clayton’s regulatory legacy closely.

What Do Reports Say About Clayton as AI Czar?

CNN reported that Trump is actively seeking to fill the AI czar position within days. Clayton currently serves as Director of National Intelligence, overseeing the 18-agency intelligence community.

Asked about the role, Trump called Clayton “a good man” and said having him take it “is a good idea.”

Clayton signaled his approach to AI oversight during his July confirmation hearing for the intelligence post. He argued that AI requires careful handling because it represents both opportunity and risk.

Former AI czar David Sacks left the position in March. His government employee status had expired, leaving the role vacant for months while Trump searched for a replacement.

No formal timeline for naming a successor has been announced publicly.

Why Does Clayton’s Ripple Lawsuit Still Matter?

Clayton led the SEC when it sued Ripple in December 2020. The agency alleged Ripple raised $1.3 billion through unregistered securities sales dating back to 2013.

A judge later found that $728.9 million in direct institutional sales qualified as unregistered offerings.

Other XRP sales, including programmatic trading, fell outside that classification.

The case closed in August 2025 with a $125 million penalty. That figure sat well under the roughly $2 billion the SEC originally sought from Ripple.

A permanent injunction still restricts how Ripple sells XRP to US institutions, even though the litigation has ended.

The lawsuit also triggered a two-and-a-half-year delisting from major exchanges. It later delayed XRP’s path to spot ETFs until November 2025, well after Bitcoin and Ethereum had already captured that institutional demand.

Crypto advocates fear Clayton could bring that same strict posture to his next role with AI regulation. Whether that caution extends to AI policy is unclear right now. No evidence suggests crypto rules would tighten under his watch.

The post Man Behind the XRP Lawsuit Could Get a White House AI Role Soon appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.description:

The post Bitget Hack Update: XRP, Bitcoin, and North Korean Link appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Chainalysis has attributed the $387 million Bitget theft to North Korean hackers. The firm said the attack lifts the value of crypto stolen by DPRK-linked actors this year above $1 billion.

North Korean attackers reportedly used a cross-chain swap to convert stolen XRP into Bitcoin and kept the tokens away from exchanges.

Drift, KelpDAO and Now Bitget

Bitget joins 2 April attacks that firms had already tied to North Korea. Hackers drained $285 million from Drift Protocol on April 1. Drift said the operation involved months of social engineering, including in-person meetings.

On April 18, attackers took $292 million through a KelpDAO bridge exploit. TRM and LayerZero both linked that attack to TraderTraitor, a Lazarus-affiliated unit.

Together, the 2 hacks made up 76% of all crypto hack losses through April, according to TRM. Chainalysis said Bitget’s $387 million brings the overall 2026 haul to over $1 billion. In 2025, DPRK actors stole over $2 billion from the crypto industry.

Chainalysis said faster tracing is becoming essential.

“The ability to quickly identify and understand illicit activity is increasingly important as North Korea increasingly uses sophisticated automation to move and obscure stolen funds,” Chainalysis said.

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen had already pointed to North Korea shortly after the breach. She cited IP addresses that matched a DPRK group’s VPN choices. The theft also ranks as 2026’s largest crypto hack, lifting September losses 462%.

How Did Stolen XRP Become Bitcoin Without an Exchange?

Chainalysis counted 23 outbound transfers in the first 3 hours after the September 24 exploit. Together, they spread $387 million across 4 blockchains.

Ethereum received nearly half the outflows at 49.7%. The XRP Ledger took 40.8%, followed by privacy-focused Zcash at 7.6% and Tron at 1.8%.

The report highlighted that instead of sending the XRP to an exchange, the attackers deposited it into a cross-chain liquidity protocol. They then withdrew Bitcoin on another network.

Chainalysis matched those deposits to their payouts. Tens of millions of dollars moved this way over roughly 36 hours. The trail ended at attacker-controlled Bitcoin addresses the firm now monitors.

Notably, the firm said it built custom automations with its in-house AI to speed up that cross-chain tracing. It estimated that more than 20 hours of manual bridge reconciliation shrank to under 10 minutes.

Investigators still set the logic and reviewed the results, Chainalysis added.

The post Bitget Hack Update: XRP, Bitcoin, and North Korean Link appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.content:encoded:
Zcash’s ETF has recorded its first week of net outflows since launching in August. Investors withdrew $93.6 million this week, as ZEC’s price fell toward $1,300.

The withdrawals mark a sharp change for Grayscale’s ZCSH fund. Just two weeks earlier, it attracted $98.2 million, leading crypto ETFs in weekly inflows. Now that demand has reversed, can Zcash hold its ground in October?

Zcash Falls as ETF Investors Withdraw

ZEC traded near $1,308 in the October 3 chart snapshot, down about 17.5% since the start of the week. It has lost roughly 23% from its recent peak near $1,690.

ETF withdrawals have accompanied that decline. The fund has recorded no daily net inflows since September 22, according to SoSoValue.

These figures suggest ETF investors have been reluctant to buy the dip. Continued withdrawals could put further pressure on ZEC, although they do not explain the entire price decline.

Zcash Price Outlook: Is the Bullish Rally Over for ZEC?

The first level to watch is $1,270–$1,300, where buyers recently stepped in. The four-hour chart’s longer-term moving average also sits near this area, making it an important test of demand.

If that support breaks, ZEC price could fall toward $1,155, roughly 12% below the chart snapshot.

The daily indicators suggest that risk remains. Buying momentum has faded, and selling pressure is still increasing.

But there is some room for optimism. Short-term selling pressure is easing, which could allow a bounce toward $1,320–$1,360.

A sustained recovery above $1,380–$1,425 would strengthen the case for a move toward $1,500 later in October.

For now, the charts favor an uneven start to the month. Holding $1,270 would give buyers time to rebuild support. Renewed ETF inflows would offer additional evidence that demand is returning.

item.content:encoded:
Jim Cramer told investors to prepare for a potentially rougher third-quarter earnings season. The Mad Money host said companies may not deliver the strong numbers investors have grown used to.

The country’s biggest lenders go first. JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Citigroup and Goldman Sachs are scheduled to report September-quarter results on October 14.

“We’re on the verge of the earnings deluge and, this time, I don’t think we’ll be getting the kind of strong numbers that we’ve become accustomed to,” Cramer stated.

Higher Rates Cloud the Q3 Earnings Season

Cramer tied his caution to rising borrowing costs and a Federal Reserve focused on bringing inflation down.

“Thanks to rising rates and [a Federal Reserve] that’s determined to bring down inflation, we’ve got a much more difficult backdrop coming up for earnings season. I’m not saying it’s impossible to make money owning stocks in this environment, but it’s certainly a lot harder than it used to be,” he said.

Cramer had already named higher rates as his biggest fear for the stock market. That concern goes back to September 16, when the Fed raised its interest rate to 4%. It was the central bank’s first hike since 2023.

Friday did bring some relief, as stocks rose on soft jobs data and falling oil prices. The Bureau of Labor Statistics said employers added 29,000 jobs in September, short of economists’ forecasts.

The unemployment rate edged up to 4.2% from 4.1% in August. Bitcoin (BTC) and gold also initially climbed after the data came out.

Analysts Remain Optimistic

Meanwhile, FactSet’s John Butters said analysts lifted S&P 500 per-share earnings estimates for Q3 by 1.4% during the quarter. Estimates typically fall during a quarter by 2.2% on average over the past 5 years.

“Heading into the start of the earnings season, analysts and companies have been more optimistic than normal in their earnings outlooks for the third quarter. As a result, estimated earnings for the S&P 500 for the third quarter are higher today compared to expectations at the start of the quarter. In addition, the index is expected to report earnings growth above 25% for the third-straight quarter,” Butters wrote.

The S&P 500 is now expected to post 29.5% year-over-year earnings growth, up from 26.7% on June 30. Of 116 companies issuing guidance, 72 issued positive outlooks and 44 negative ones.

Investors will also hear from New York Fed President John Williams on Tuesday. In Buffalo on September 29, he said the Fed did not need to rush another hike. He added that one more may suit late this year.

The weak payrolls now give Williams fresh data to address. The October 14 bank results will then begin the main test of profits under higher borrowing costs. They will also show whether analysts were right to raise their forecasts.

item.content:encoded:
Most of the crypto market drifted lower into early October. However, Pump.fun (PUMP), Aave (AAVE), Worldcoin (WLD), and Sky (SKY) went the other way.

Santiment ties three of the rallies to project news, including token buybacks, Aave’s lending growth, and a Galaxy Digital development.

Why 4 Altcoins are Rallying

Total crypto market capitalization slipped only 0.30% over the past week, according to BeInCrypto Markets.

On Friday, Bitcoin saw a massive rally from $84,000 to $87,000, but crashed back to the early levels almost immediately. Market sentiment toward ETH and XRP turned negative as October began.

Meanwhile, AAVE posted 20% gains, including a 7% jump on Friday. This is largely due to the Aave protocol reaching the $1 billion milestone in user deposits.

V4 also went live on Arc and Base in September. On Base, an Equities Hub lets eligible non-US users borrow USDC (USDC) against 7 Coinbase-tokenized US stocks.

Pump.fun also rallied 30% in a week, and it was largely due to the token’s supply cuts.

“Pump.fun is directing roughly half of net protocol revenue into PUMP buybacks and burns, with daily purchases topping $1M several times in late September,” the firm said.

Together with Hyperliquid, Pump.fun drove nearly 90% of the record $638 million in token buybacks, BeInCrypto reported in August.

Santiment tied SKY’s 14% weekly gain to rising institutional interest. Last month, Galaxy Digital said it had added $100 million of sUSDS, Sky’s yield-bearing savings token, to its treasury.

Galaxy also approved sUSDS as collateral across its institutional trading business and bought an undisclosed amount of SKY. Lastly, Worldcoin added 15% this week. Santiment did not tie that move to a specific catalyst.

Quant Gives Back Part of Its Clearing House Price Rally

Santiment named Quant (QNT) among the tokens that fell the hardest in early October. The altcoin dropped 7% on Friday, a move the firm attributed to profit-taking after a steep rally. 

Since its late September high, QNT has declined over 32%. Despite this, it remains up 152% over 7 days at $252.55, BeInCrypto Markets data show. 

Santiment framed the red week as a test of traders’ appetite for early October dips. Next week’s performance will show whether the selloff continues or the market turns.

The post Crypto's Layoff List Grows as Anchorage Digital Reportedly Trims 17% of Its Workforce appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered US digital asset bank, has reportedly laid off 17% of its staff. Chief Executive Nathan McCauley told employees about the cuts this week, according to The Information.

The report cited people familiar with the matter and tied the layoffs to a year-long crypto market slump. Anchorage has not publicly commented on the reduction.

How Many Jobs Anchorage’s 17% Cut Could Reach

McCauley put the global workforce at about 400 people in congressional testimony in February 2025. If staffing held near that level, a 17% cut would affect roughly 68 jobs.

The real figure may differ since headcount could have shifted since then. BeInCrypto has contacted Anchorage Digital for comment.

The company has made deep cuts before. In 2023, Anchorage laid off 20% of its workforce. McCauley later said that being cut off from banks contributed to that decision.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

From Bitwise to Coinbase, Crypto’s Job Cuts Keep Coming

Anchorage joins a long line of crypto firms that have cut staff in 2026. Gemini shrank its workforce by about 30%, while Crypto.com cut 12% in March.

Coinbase then announced it is eliminating about 700 roles, or 14% of staff, in May. That same month, Dune laid off 25% of its team to focus on AI agents and institutional data.

Exchange Luno trimmed 20% of its staff in July, and Bitwise cut about 14% in August. Others announced complete shutdowns, including BitMEX, the Lisk blockchain, and Ethereum layer-2 network Blast.

Outside crypto, technology companies have stepped up job cuts. US tech firms announced 10,799 cuts in September, up 77% from August, a Challenger, Gray & Christmas report shows.

Tech has announced 165,925 cuts so far in 2026, up 54% from a year earlier. However, total US job cut announcements fell 18% in September, leaving tech with 29% of this year’s cuts.

item.title: Citadel Says Wall Street’s Biggest Buyers Are Ready to Reload Stocks in Q4
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Citadel Securities says retail traders, buybacks, and quant funds will reload stocks in Q4. Here is the case and the risks.

The post Citadel Says Wall Street’s Biggest Buyers Are Ready to Reload Stocks in Q4 appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Small investors walked away from US stocks in September. Now the firm that handles about 35% of their trades says they are about to come back.

“September was the reset. Q4 is the reload,” Scott Rubner, a strategist at Citadel Securities, wrote to clients on Thursday.

The catch? The call lands as US hiring slows sharply, borrowing costs top 5%, and most stocks fell last month.

The Buyers Who Went Quiet

Retail share trading fell to 0.94 times its one-year average in September, the lowest of 2026, according to Bloomberg. That is 26% below June’s peak.

Retail trading has risen from September to October in each of the past four years, by about 8% on average.

Companies are next. Most cannot buy back their own shares before earnings, and those windows reopen October 15.

Model-driven trading funds have cut their stock bets to the bottom fifth of their range since 2024.

Analysts expect S&P 500 earnings per share to jump 27% this quarter, and Goldman Sachs has dismissed talk of an S&P 500 earnings bubble.

“The story in 2026 has not been a low bar. Expectations have moved higher, and companies have continued to clear them by a wide margin,” Rubner told clients.

Why the Reload Could Misfire

History helps, but it is bumpy. Since 1930, the S&P 500 has averaged a 5.6% gain in the fourth quarter of midterm-election years, almost double the usual 2.9%.

Yet in 14 of those 23 years, the quarter’s low came in October.

“A constructive Q4 setup does not necessarily mean a clean start to October.”

The economy looks shakier. US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, against forecasts of 84,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%.

The rally is also thin. BeInCrypto reported that most S&P 500 stocks fell in September, even as the index edged higher.

And consider the messenger. Citadel Securities makes money executing trades, including the retail orders it expects to return.

“September took leverage and positioning out. Q4 brings earnings, catalysts, and buyers back in,” Rubner concluded.

The first test comes October 15.

item.content:encoded:
Nvidia stock finally broke through on October 2. Shares hit a new all-time intraday high of about $237.83, overtaking the previous May record.

The immediate catalyst came from Morgan Stanley. Analyst Joseph Moore restored Nvidia as the firm’s top semiconductor pick after meetings with CEO Jensen Huang and CFO Colette Kress. 

Why Nvidia Stock Price Surged to a Record High

Morgan Stanley kept its Overweight rating and $300 price target, pointing to Nvidia’s new product cycle and growing demand from AI labs and agentic AI.

The wider market helped. A weaker-than-expected US jobs report pushed investors away from expectations for another near-term Federal Reserve rate hike. The Nasdaq also reached record territory.

Nvidia had another tailwind already in place. On September 28, the company added $150 billion to its share-buyback authorization, taking the remaining program to $235 billion. 

Huang said the move reflected Nvidia’s “confidence in the long-term opportunity ahead.”

Nvidia Stock Price Outlook from Wall Street Giants

The striking part is that the record price remains below nearly every major Wall Street target.

Recent analyst actions support those targets.

Across 61 analysts tracked by S&P Global, Nvidia’s average target is now $327.70. That implies roughly 40% upside from Friday’s close.

That optimism still carries a high bar. Goldman Sachs has previously warned that expectations around Nvidia are elevated. Investors now need continued evidence that AI spending can support the valuation.

What Nvidia Investors Should Watch Next

  • November — Q3 earnings: Nvidia has not yet announced the exact date. Rubin demand, revenue guidance and margins will matter most.
  • Rubin and Vera rollout: Morgan Stanley sees the new product cycle and agentic AI as major potential growth drivers.
  • AI spending: Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and other large customers need to keep pouring money into infrastructure.
  • The $235 billion buyback: Nvidia plans to execute the remaining authorization through fiscal 2028.

item.title: Netflix Stock Lost Nearly 50% of Its Value in a Year. Will It Keep Falling?
item.dc:creator: Jakub Dziadkowiec
item.description:
Netflix stock tests its 2021 peak near $68 after Ted Sarandos admits growth is slowing ahead of October 20 earnings.

The post Netflix Stock Lost Nearly 50% of Its Value in a Year. Will It Keep Falling? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Netflix stock trades near $68, roughly half its June 2025 record of $134. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos admitted on Thursday that the streamer is growing more slowly than he wants.

Sarandos blames the slowdown largely on Netflix’s own spending choices. However, a growing camp of investors sees a bigger threat in rivals with far deeper pockets.

Why is Netflix Stock Dropping?

Speaking at Bloomberg’s Screentime event in Los Angeles, Sarandos named live programming as a key drag on growth.

“Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to… We are, though, also doing things that create a lot of headwind.”

Ted Sarandos, co-CEO of Netflix, via Yahoo

Live events absorb about 5% of Netflix’s $20 billion annual content budget. Yet they generate only around 1% of total viewing hours.

Overall viewership rose just 2% year over year in the first half of 2026.

Not everyone accepts that explanation. Investor Stock Market Nerd argued that live content attracts a disproportionate share of new, engaged members, which should offset the cost.

Can a Pure-Play Streamer Outspend Big Tech?

Instead, the investor blames competition from Apple, Amazon, and Alphabet. These giants can fund streaming libraries without needing them to earn much profit.

Amazon alone is valued near $3 trillion, roughly 10 times Netflix’s $285 billion market cap.

Viewing data supports the concern. YouTube captured a record 14.2% of US TV viewing in July, according to TheStreet.

By contrast, Netflix held 7.9% in June, per Nielsen’s last reading before a methodology change.

Meanwhile, Wall Street is split. Wells Fargo cut Netflix to underweight on September 18 with a $57 target, while HSBC moved to hold.

Deutsche Bank upgraded the stock to buy on September 30, setting a $95 target and citing 18% Asia-Pacific revenue growth.

Guidance explains the caution. Netflix’s next-quarter revenue growth forecasts slipped from 15% to 13% to 12% across 2026, according to Fool.

Netflix Stock Price Outlook

Since the June 2025 record, NFLX has printed lower highs and lower lows on the weekly chart. It now tests the November 2021 peak near $68.

Just below sits the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement at $61.29, a level traders use to gauge pullback depth. Together, they form a support band.

Overhead, the lost 0.382 Fibonacci level at $89.10 now acts as resistance. The falling 50-week moving average sits near the same zone.

The weekly Relative Strength Index (RSI) shows a bullish divergence. The stock is heading towards oversold levels. Price set lower lows in February and July, while RSI set higher lows.

A third drive would likely require a dip below the $65.08 July low. A sustained break under $61. If that happens, Netflix Stock could be heading towards $41.

Netflix is down about 27% this year, even as the S&P 500 set a record high in August. The October 20 report may decide whether investors still value a pure-play streamer competing against companies that treat content as a side business.

The post Netflix Stock Lost Nearly 50% of Its Value in a Year. Will It Keep Falling? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: US Rallied Bitcoin and Iran Crashed It In a Dramatic 24 Hours for Crypto
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Bitcoin fell from $87,000 as UKMTO reported a Hormuz tanker attack. Oil held steady. Here is what the data shows.

The post US Rallied Bitcoin and Iran Crashed It In a Dramatic 24 Hours for Crypto appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin price started Friday, October 1, at $84,000. Then, disappointing US jobs data and falling Fed rate-hike odds triggered a bullish rally for BTC, taking the token near $87,000.

However, Bitcoin now ends the day at the same price it started, adding and losing $50 billion in a single day. So, what caused this volatility?

According to a British maritime agency, Iran struck a massive oil tanker in Hormuz, making it the sixth tanker attack this week. Oil prices barely flinched, but crypto markets reacted heavily.

Hormuz Remains a Decisive Factor for Markets

United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), the Royal Navy-run center that tracks threats to merchant ships, issued its warning on Friday.

A tanker’s master reported the hit at 11:22 UTC during an outbound transit. The impact sparked a small fire and knocked out power on board.

The crew put out the fire, and the ship kept moving. UKMTO reported no casualties or pollution.

The agency did not name the vessel or the attacker. Viral posts on X (Twitter) blamed Iran. UKMTO said only that authorities are investigating.

A day earlier, the Kuwait-flagged supertanker Kazimah III caught fire after a similar strike. Vessels faced at least 16 attacks in the strait in September, according to Seatrade.

Why Oil Held Steady While Bitcoin Fell

Binance data shows the Bitcoin price rejected near $87,000 for the third time in two weeks, after tops on September 22 and 23.

Crude told a calmer story. US crude spot traded near $93.70 and Brent spot near $106.30, each up less than 0.25% on the latest candles.

Brent futures had already fallen 2.89% to $99.35 earlier Friday, according to The National. Reports that the European Union and International Energy Agency (IEA) members were weighing stockpile releases drove that drop.

“Renewed US military deployments to the region kept the risk premium alive,” said Daniel Richards, senior economist at Emirates NBD.

Those deployments are growing. Washington has sent two more Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar and is moving a third carrier strike group into the region, Axios reported.

President Donald Trump has also said he is weighing renewed bombing, a threat that has shadowed oil and Bitcoin markets for weeks.

Traders now face a test of whether Bitcoin can clear $87,000 while the strait remains under fire.

item.content:encoded:
Are quantum computers still years away from breaking modern encryption at scale? Or is Q-Day almost here? Regardless of the answer, Governments are no longer waiting.

On Friday, BeInCrypto led the regulatory discussion on Quantum risks at the UN Headquarters during the Government Blockchain Association’s Future of Money, Governance and the Law summit.

But why now? Because the US National Security Agency announced a major shift toward post-quantum cryptography. From 2027, new commercial national-security systems must support quantum-resistant algorithms. Incompatible systems will be phased out by 2030. 

The fear is already here: attackers can steal encrypted data today and wait for future quantum machines to crack it.

The UN Pension Fund Is Already Preparing

Brian McGleenon spoke with IRS Chief Risk and Control Officer Dottie Romo, UN Joint Staff Pension Fund Deputy Chief Executive Dino Cataldo Dell’Accio, and Mastercard’s Julius Moye.

Dell’Accio revealed that quantum migration is already a live issue for the UN pension fund’s blockchain-based proof-of-life system, serving roughly 80,000 beneficiaries across 190 countries.

We have been in production for five years. The concern now is what happens to information already written to a blockchain if today’s cryptography becomes vulnerable.”

The fund is exploring a post-quantum-resistant blockchain and ways to re-encrypt and publicly anchor historical records.

His key warning: there may be no clean “Q-Day” when institutions simply upgrade and move on.

There is no such a day as a Y2K in quantum. Cryptography will require continuous monitoring as threats evolve.”

The Threat Starts Before Q-Day

The NSA calls this “harvest now, decrypt later.” NIST is already urging organizations to migrate to finalized post-quantum standards rather than wait for powerful quantum computers to arrive.

Dell’Accio flagged another problem. Quantum-safe cryptographic keys can be much larger, meaning existing firewalls, network hardware and software may need upgrades too.

Finance May Have a Speed Problem

IRS Officer Dottie Romo ended with a broader warning about regulation.

“Right now we’re reviewing things at a very traditional pace,” Romo said. “That’s not going to be sustainable.”

Quantum may still be ahead of us. The race to protect the financial system has already started.
